owner_creation.analysis: src/safe_core/bytebuf.rs owns ByteBuf and adapter vectors independently. At 16-23 ByteBuf and NulTerminatedBytes each own a private Vec<u8>; construction copies caller bytes after a successful fallible reserve.
owner_creation.invariant: Each byte vector has one Rust object owner.
limitations: Pure component review only; this does not approve legacy xbuffer callers or integrate ByteBuf into either production executable.
ByteBuf storage is separate from any NulTerminatedBytes adapter allocation.

aliases_escapes.analysis: src/safe_core/bytebuf.rs restricts escaping access to borrowed slices. As_bytes returns only shared borrowed slices; self-copy APIs accept ranges and reacquire bytes after reserve instead of retaining a pointer into the old Vec.
aliases_escapes.invariant: A retained slice cannot coexist with mutation in safe Rust.
limitations: Borrow checking protects safe slices; no native raw-pointer consumer is analyzed here.

callback_targets.analysis: src/safe_core/bytebuf.rs uses synchronous reserve gates. Gate::before_reserve and the interior-NUL predicate are synchronous Rust calls; no native string callback or pointer is registered.
callback_targets.invariant: Reserve gates do not retain borrowed byte storage.
limitations: ReserveFault behavior is component testing, not pager callback wiring.

invalidation.analysis: src/safe_core/bytebuf.rs reacquires self-copy data after reserve. Reset/truncate/pop preserve Vec ownership; replacement stages a distinct Vec and self-copy uses original indices after any reallocation.
invalidation.invariant: Growth cannot invalidate an escaped raw alias.

mutation_commit.analysis: src/safe_core/bytebuf.rs stages replacement before changing self.bytes. At 102-121 replacement reserves and fills staged storage before assigning self.bytes; the old owner survives an allocation failure unchanged.
mutation_commit.invariant: Replacement commits only a complete staged vector.

release_pair.analysis: src/safe_core/bytebuf.rs drops replaced vectors through Rust ownership. Assignment drops the replaced Vec once; the C-string adapter returns a separately owned vector, so dropping ByteBuf cannot retire its adapter.
release_pair.invariant: Adapter storage has an independent Rust release path.
limitations: Rust Vec destruction is relied on; no native allocator pair is implied.

error_cleanup.analysis: src/safe_core/bytebuf.rs returns typed errors before exposing partial bytes. Range, length and interior-NUL errors return small StorageError values; failed reserve never exposes uninitialized bytes or partial content.
error_cleanup.invariant: Error returns preserve the previous initialized byte sequence.

signals_handoff.analysis: src/safe_core/bytebuf.rs permits mutation only through exclusive Rust borrows. Exclusive mutation uses &mut self and the crate forbids unsafe code; no handler entry or global scratch buffer exists in this component.
signals_handoff.invariant: Byte-owner mutation belongs to normal Rust control flow.

src/safe_core/mod.rs.relationship: The root attribute at src/safe_core/mod.rs:1-3 forbids unsafe code for the isolated component crate containing ByteBuf; this supports the safe-borrow scope, not pager integration.
